facts.text: Thendara station once served as the northern terminus for Adirondack Railroad trains coming from Utica until the line extended to Tupper Lake in 2023.
The hamlet’s name originated from the nearby Fulton Chain of Lakes, which early settlers called “Fulton Chain” after the famed steamboat inventor.
Located within the Fulton Chain Wild Forest, Thendara sits at elevations between 1,700 and 2,500 feet, surrounded by mixed hardwoods that shift to coniferous stands higher up.
The area’s geology features Precambrian bedrock over a billion years old, shaped by glaciers that left erratics and carved the valleys that now host the Fulton Chain of Lakes.
